profile.reading:
This footprint is the 2403 Walsh Avenue building of Csquare's SFO1 in Santa Clara, California. The distinction matters because SFO1 is two buildings and the registry holds both. Geocoding 2403 Walsh Avenue lands within about 40 feet of this record's coordinates, while 2401 Walsh Avenue sits roughly 350 feet north and is mapped as a separate way. The City of Santa Clara parcel layer returns assessor parcel 216-28-126 here, zoned LI for light industrial, general plan light industrial, in Council District 1, with a construction year of 1973. The 2401 Walsh parcel next door, 216-28-127, is dated 1997. A 1973 industrial shell later filled with raised floor is a very Silicon Valley provenance and it is worth knowing that the two halves of SFO1 are a quarter century apart in age.

Csquare, Inc. trades on the New York Stock Exchange as CSQR. Its Silicon Valley buildings descend from CenturyLink and Savvis heritage colocation assets that were divested around 2020 and 2021, became Evoque Data Center Solutions under Brookfield affiliated ownership, were renamed Centersquare, and were renamed again to Csquare ahead of an initial public offering on 16 July 2026 that priced 50 million shares at 21 dollars for roughly 1.05 billion dollars gross, after which Brookfield Corporation retained about 69 percent of voting power, making Csquare a controlled company under NYSE rules. The registration prospectus reports a portfolio as of 31 March 2026 of 64 sites in 21 metros across the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom, roughly 389 megawatts of sellable power capacity and more than 1,700 customers. Its properties table splits this site into SFO1_A at 60,982 rentable square feet and 64.9 percent occupied and SFO1_B at 38,634 rentable square feet and 63.9 percent occupied, both company owned. Which suffix corresponds to which street address is not stated, so no floor area is written to this row.

On the power side Csquare is unusually careful with its own wording, and the registry follows it. Its Silicon Valley page gives SFO1 as 95,981 square feet of raised floor with, in its own words, utility power of 34.5 MW. That is the service the pair of buildings can draw, not IT load and not this building alone. The same page gives the four building Silicon Valley cluster as more than 273,000 square feet of raised floor and 129.4 MW of combined utility power, made up of SFO1 at 34.5 MW, SFO2 in Santa Clara at 43.2 MW, SFO3 in Sunnyvale at 8.6 MW and SFO4 in Santa Clara at 43.1 MW.

Santa Clara is the reason a building like this exists where it does. The city runs its own municipal electric utility, Silicon Valley Power, whose December 2025 fact sheet reports a peak demand of 746.5 MW across 62,447 electric accounts in an 18.41 square mile service area. Silicon Valley Power says the city hosts more than 50 data centres and that 53 percent of its power use and sales come from them. That concentration has hit a ceiling. In May 2025 the utility's chief operating officer told San Jose Spotlight that operators had asked to add 500 megawatts of load against a peak of about 720, and a city spokesperson said the electrical grid caps new data centre approvals and that expansion projects were estimated to finish by 2029.

What is not known: which of SFO1_A and SFO1_B is this building, its individual floor area, any IT load figure at all, and its tenants, none of which Csquare publishes at building level.

reading:
Csquare is the current name of a Brookfield backed colocation platform assembled from two predecessor businesses, and as of July 2026 it is a listed company rather than a private one. Evoque Data Center Solutions was formed by Brookfield in 2019 out of the data centre assets AT&T divested. Cyxtera Technologies, which had been spun out of CenturyLink infrastructure in 2017, filed for Chapter 11 in June 2023, and Brookfield bought its assets for 775 million dollars in a deal that completed in January 2024. The combined business launched as Centersquare in April 2024 and now trades as Csquare, from 3100 Olympus Boulevard, Suite 510, Coppell, Texas. This registry carries separate rows for Cyxtera and Centersquare, which are earlier names for the same company rather than separate operators.

The public record is now unusually complete because of the offering. Csquare, Inc. filed a Form S-1 on 16 June 2026, was declared effective on 15 July, and filed its final prospectus on 16 July. That prospectus records 50,000,000 shares at 21.00 dollars, gross proceeds of 1.05 billion dollars and about 1.01 billion dollars to the company before expenses, a New York Stock Exchange listing under CSQR, and Brookfield holding roughly 69.0 percent of voting power afterwards, which makes Csquare a controlled company under exchange rules. As of 31 March 2026 the prospectus describes 64 completed and operating data centres across 21 metropolitan markets in the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom, 35 owned and 29 leased, delivering approximately 389 MW of what the company defines as sellable power capacity, with more than 36,600 interconnection products sold. The business is deliberately small footprint, focused on deployments below 5 MW, averaging about 7.6 contracted kilowatts per rack, with some installations as high as 150 kilowatts per rack. Csquare estimates roughly 670 MW of further capacity could be added inside its existing buildings, 330 MW from equipment optimisation and 340 MW under roof, at about 4 billion dollars of capital expenditure.

Everything the registry holds for this row is in one market. Silicon Valley accounted for about 13 percent of portfolio annualised recurring revenue at 31 March 2026, and the seven stored buildings are SFO1 at 2401 and 2403 Walsh Avenue in Santa Clara, SFO2 at 4650 and 4700 Old Ironsides Drive in Santa Clara, SFO4 at 1500 and 1550 Space Park Drive in Santa Clara, and SFO3 at 1400 Kifer Road in Sunnyvale. The apparent duplicate pairs are not duplicates. They are the separate buildings holding the A and B halls that the prospectus lists individually, with sellable and sold capacity given per hall.

Csquare's own Silicon Valley page separates the power numbers properly, which is rare. SFO1 has 95,981 square feet of raised floor behind 34.5 MW of utility power, 11.2 MW of UPS capacity and 17.5 MW of generator capacity. SFO2 has 100,056 square feet behind 43.2 MW utility, 14.1 MW UPS and 22.5 MW generator. SFO4 has 57,450 square feet behind 43.1 MW utility, 12.3 MW UPS and 20.5 MW generator. SFO3 in Sunnyvale has 19,661 square feet behind 8.6 MW utility, 3.2 MW UPS and 5 MW generator. The market total the company gives is more than 273,000 square feet and 129.4 MW of utility power. None of those is an IT load figure, and the utility number is the service the buildings can draw, not what they consume.

The local record is the electricity. The four Santa Clara buildings sit inside the service territory of Silicon Valley Power, the city owned utility, which states that Santa Clara hosts more than 50 data centres and that 53 percent of its power use and sales come from them.
